findings: `getDashboard` awaits `fetchLivePrice` sequentially inside a `for` loop instead of issuing the calls concurrently (e.g. `Promise.all`), so total latency scales linearly with the number of orders — an O(n) chain of network round-trips per request.
`pricingApi.get(sku)` is called with no timeout configured on the client, so any single slow or hung upstream call blocks that iteration indefinitely with no way to time out.

`fetchLivePrice` retries on `catch (e)` unconditionally, calling itself again with `await fetchLivePrice(sku)` — there is no maximum retry count, so a persistently failing/hanging pricing API causes unbounded (potentially infinite) retries for that SKU.

The retry has no backoff/jitter — it re-issues the request immediately in a tight loop, which under load turns a single slow dependency into a retry storm that amplifies pressure on `pricingApi` (thundering-herd/retry-amplification), making the outage worse for all concurrent dashboard requests.

The retry does not distinguish error types — it retries identically on network errors, timeouts, and permanent client errors (e.g. invalid SKU / 4xx), so non-retryable errors are retried forever with no chance of success, wasting resources and never surfacing the failure.

Because there is no timeout and no retry cap, a single bad order/SKU can make the entire `getDashboard` call hang indefinitely — there is no overall request-level timeout/deadline wrapping the whole function, so the endpoint's 'occasional timeout' symptom is really 'never returns' for that request.

`db.query('SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id=$1', ...)` has no LIMIT/pagination, so a user with a large order history pulls an unbounded result set into memory and drives an unbounded number of sequential `fetchLivePrice` calls.
`SELECT *` fetches all columns even though only `order` fields plus `price` are used downstream, adding unnecessary I/O/network overhead per row.

There is no caching of live prices, so if multiple orders share the same SKU (or the same dashboard is requested repeatedly in a short window), identical pricing lookups are re-fetched from the upstream API every time instead of being reused.

The `db.query` call itself has no try/catch or timeout — a slow or failing DB call has the same unbounded-hang risk as the pricing calls, and any DB error propagates as an unhandled rejection from `getDashboard` with no context added.

There's no concurrency cap even if the sequential loop were parallelized — naively switching to `Promise.all` over all orders would fire unbounded simultaneous requests at `pricingApi`, which is itself a scalability/thundering-herd risk without a batching/concurrency-limit strategy.

No circuit breaker around `pricingApi` — a degraded/down pricing service is retried the same way regardless of how many recent calls have already failed, rather than failing fast once the dependency is known to be unhealthy.
